payload.title: Kubo S3 datastore has empty credentials — can't read blocks from R2
payload.description: The ipfs config Datastore.Spec.mounts[0].child has accessKey='' and secretKey=''. The R2 IPFS credentials exist in env vars (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY from R2_IPFS_ACCESS_KEY/R2_IPFS_SECRET_KEY) but the kubo S3 datastore plugin reads from the ipfs config file, not env vars. The kubo container start script needs to write these into the config before starting the daemon. Without this, kubo can't read blocks from the dumpster-ipfs R2 bucket and all image fetches via media.dumpster.cash time out.

payload.title: Frontend shows 1 of 3 tokens despite API returning all 3
payload.description: GET /tokens returns all 3 tokens with correct data. The frontend only renders 1. Likely a Next.js SSR/hydration issue or a client-side rendering bug. Not related to deployment changes.

payload.title: Kubo leveldb metadata lost on pod restart — S3 blocks unreachable
payload.description: go-ds-s3 stores blocks in R2 but the DAG/pin index lives in local leveldb at $IPFS_PATH/datastore. This is ephemeral storage. After pod restart, kubo has S3 credentials and can reach R2, but doesn't know which blocks exist there — the leveldb index is gone. Kubo falls back to network resolution which times out. Fix: add a PVC for $IPFS_PATH or switch to a datastore that keeps the full index in S3. Credential injection (ds-a1a) is necessary but not sufficient.

payload.comment: Corrected diagnosis: all 3 tokens render in ticker and featured card. The bug is that the filtered grid view under New/Runners/etc tabs shows 'No tokens found'. The filter query returns empty despite 3 active tokens existing. This is a frontend API call or filter logic bug, not a rendering issue.
